hacoo-links-not-working.title: Hacoo Links Not Working: App Redirects and Missing Products
hacoo-links-not-working.description: Diagnose Hacoo links that open the app home screen, lose the selected item or show an unavailable product, with a practical record of each result.

sections.title: Identify the failed step before changing anything
body: When a Hacoo link does not work, start by identifying where the journey stops. A browser error, an app home screen, a missing product and an unavailable size are four different results. Write down the original URL, where you opened it, the final screen and the time. This small record prevents a changed destination from being mistaken for a working product link.

This guide is an independent troubleshooting method, not a description of Hacoo’s internal routing system. It does not establish why any particular listing disappeared. Its aim is to help you isolate the failure, keep a useful product reference and decide whether the next step belongs in the browser, the app or an existing order. Work with one link at a time and stop repeating a test once it produces the same result.

sections.title: A link opens the app home screen
body: An app opening successfully does not mean that the product destination survived the handoff. Record that the result was the home screen, then return to the original message or saved entry. Check that you copied the complete link rather than its visible caption. If the link is split across lines, make sure punctuation from the surrounding sentence was not included. Do not guess missing characters or change the product identifier.

If the operating system offers an ordinary choice between opening the browser and the installed app, try the intended official app once. After any normal sign-in requested by the app, reopen the original link rather than searching from memory. Compare the resulting image, title and variant with the saved reference. If the app still opens only its home screen, mark the link unresolved; opening a generic screen is not a successful product match.

sections.title: A link works in one context but fails in another
body: Keep the same destination and change only one context at a time. For example, compare a link opened inside a messaging app with the same complete link opened in your regular browser. Record the browser, operating system and installed app version. A difference between those two attempts helps describe the problem, but it does not prove which service caused it. Avoid making several settings changes before you have one reproducible observation.

Do not begin by deleting all app data or reinstalling. Those actions can remove useful local state and make the original failure harder to describe. Check for an ordinary update through the official app store and preserve the original URL first. If the issue began after an update, keep the version and time in your notes. A replacement download from an unknown site is not a reliable way to repair a product route.

sections.title: The product is missing or marked unavailable
body: A missing listing needs a different conclusion from a failed app launch. Check whether the page contains an explicit availability message, whether only one color or size is unavailable, and whether the saved product title still appears. Use the same account and actual delivery region throughout the comparison. Another person’s screenshot shows their own viewing context and time; it does not demonstrate availability for your account today.

Do not change your delivery country simply to make a product appear. A visible listing and a deliverable order are separate facts. If the original product cannot be reproduced, label the saved entry unavailable or changed with the date. A visually similar search result can be kept as an alternative, but it needs its own URL, measurements and option check. Never silently substitute that alternative into a record of the original item.

sections.title: An existing order is different from a discovery link
body: If you have already paid, begin in the order history rather than relying on a public product link. Record the selected option, quantity and current order status there. A public listing becoming unavailable does not by itself tell you whether the order is cancelled, dispatched or still being prepared. Keep the transaction record separate from the discovery page so a change to one does not erase the evidence in the other.

Use the support route attached to that order when the problem concerns fulfilment or the item received. Describe the discrepancy precisely: for example, the original public link is unavailable while the order still shows processing. Ask which current status applies to the order. Do not place another order merely because an old link failed, and do not treat a missing public listing as confirmation that a refund has been approved.

sections.title: Repair the spreadsheet entry without losing its history
body: A useful Hacoo spreadsheet should distinguish verified, changed and unresolved entries. Keep the original URL, last check date, final destination and selected option in separate fields. If you publish a collection, remove misleading availability claims as soon as a route can no longer be reproduced. Keeping a dated explanation is more helpful than presenting every saved image as a currently purchasable product.

For example, an entry might read: checked 12 October, app opened at home, product not confirmed, original link retained privately for another check. That is an illustrative record, not a report about a tested Hacoo item. Once a route is verified again, compare image, title and option before changing its status. Do not update the check date just because the page was edited; the date should describe an actual inspection of that destination.

sections.title: Prepare one reproducible support report
body: For an unresolved technical issue, collect the complete public link, the opening context, device and operating system, app version, actual country and the visible result. Explain the shortest sequence that reproduces it. A report saying that a link from a message opens the app home screen after sign-in is more useful than saying that the whole app is broken. Add a screenshot only when it shows the relevant screen clearly.

Keep private order identifiers in the official support conversation. Remove addresses, payment details and unrelated messages from any public screenshot. Support should not need your password or verification code to understand a link problem. Ask one concrete question, such as whether the route is still available to your account, and keep the response with the original record. A clear report helps investigation; it does not guarantee restoration of the listing.

sections.title: Finish with a clear outcome and a useful next page
body: End the check with one of three outcomes: the intended product opened and matched, a different destination opened, or the product could not be confirmed. Record the evidence that supports that outcome. Avoid vague labels such as fixed when you have only reached a category or home screen. A failed link can remain unresolved without requiring a speculative explanation about stock, moderation or the platform’s internal systems.

Use the spreadsheet guide for maintaining product references, the website-versus-app guide for choosing the right interface, and the region-access guide for account-specific visibility. For a paid order, use the order-tracking or returns guide instead. These tasks are related, but they are not interchangeable. Resolving the right stage of the journey makes the next click useful and keeps a broken discovery link from becoming a mistaken conclusion about an order.

hacoo-shoe-size-guide.title: Hacoo Shoe Size Guide: Foot Length, Width and Fit Checks
hacoo-shoe-size-guide.description: Compare foot measurements with the exact Hacoo shoe listing, distinguish EU/UK/US labels from centimetres and document fit before normal wear.

sections.title: Start with the chart for the exact shoe
body: A Hacoo shoe size guide should begin with the actual listing and its selected variant. EU, UK and US labels are useful references, but they are not a substitute for a product-specific measurement chart. Two listings using the same size label may describe different shapes or use different measurement conventions. Save the chart, unit, variant and date before deciding which option to choose.

This guide provides a repeatable measuring method rather than a universal Hacoo conversion table. It does not claim that every shoe uses one brand’s sizing. If a listing gives only a size label, record that the underlying measurements are missing. A familiar number is a starting point for comparison, not proof of comfort. Keeping that uncertainty visible is especially useful when the shoe’s construction differs from the pair you normally wear.

sections.title: Measure both feet under comparable conditions
body: Use a flat floor, paper, a straight edge and a ruler marked in centimetres or millimetres. Wear the type of socks you expect to use. Stand naturally with weight on both feet, keeping the heel position consistent, and mark the longest toe and the back of the heel. Measure the straight distance between those points. Repeat the process on the other foot and repeat any surprising result.

Record both values instead of averaging them away. Also note the method and date so a later comparison uses the same conditions. A measurement taken while seated or with the paper moving is not directly comparable with a standing measurement. If another person helps, make sure the marks describe the foot rather than the outline of a thick pen held at an angle. Small technique differences can matter when choosing between nearby options.

sections.title: Keep foot length, insole length and outsole length separate
body: Read the listing’s chart heading carefully. A value may describe the wearer’s foot, the removable insole or the outside sole. These are different measurements and should not be compared as if they were interchangeable. A longer outsole does not reveal the usable space inside the shoe, and a removable insole may not describe the whole internal shape. If the chart does not define its measurement, ask for clarification before relying on it.

Do not add a fixed allowance automatically. Use any fitting instruction supplied for that particular product and keep it separate from your measured foot length. An illustrative comparison might record a 26.0 cm foot and a chart field whose meaning is unknown; the correct action is to resolve that field, not assume that 26.0 cm means the same thing in both records. The example is a method, not a size recommendation.

sections.title: Account for width, toe shape and intended use
body: Length is only one part of fit. Record whether the toe box shape, forefoot width, heel hold and instep space resemble a pair that already works for you. A narrow shoe and a wider shoe can share the same labelled size while feeling different. Product photographs may help identify shape, but they cannot establish the internal width or how the upper will behave on your foot.

Keep intended use in the comparison. Socks, an orthotic, a removable insole or the need for extra room can change what matters. Do not assume a material will stretch enough to correct a poor fit. Record any statement about material as a listing claim, and distinguish it from an observation you have made. If a critical width or construction detail is unavailable, leave the decision open rather than hiding the gap behind a size conversion.

sections.title: Read fit reviews as contextual evidence
body: A review saying true to size is useful only when its context is clear. Look for the exact model, selected size, usual comparison pair and the reviewer’s description of length or width. A comment about a different shoe or another production period can suggest a question, but it is not a measurement of your chosen option. Separate reviews about comfort from those about delivery or customer service.

Prefer specific observations, such as heel movement or pressure across the forefoot, over a general approval. Photographs should belong to the reviewed variant and show what the reviewer is describing. Do not combine measurements from several unrelated reviews into an invented official chart. Your decision record should show which facts came from the listing, which came from your own measurement and which remain another person’s experience.

sections.title: Confirm the chosen option again in the cart
body: After selecting a size, verify the color, size label, quantity and whether the item is a single pair or a bundle. A page can return to a default option when reopened. Recheck the chart attached to the selected variant rather than a screenshot from an earlier candidate. If the chart changes with the option, keep the final version that actually informed the decision.

A compact comparison record needs the listing URL, chart date, measured left and right foot lengths, the chart’s measurement definition, selected size and one unresolved point. Add the expected use or width requirement only where relevant. This record is more useful than collecting dozens of unlabelled screenshots. Before payment, review the current order terms and decide whether any remaining measurement gap is important enough to pause the purchase.

sections.title: Check the delivered pair before normal wear
body: When the shoes arrive, confirm that both size labels and the selected color match the order. Inspect the pair for visible differences and keep the packaging while you make the initial assessment. Try them in a clean indoor setting where appropriate under the current return conditions. Compare heel hold, toe space and pressure with the fit you intended, using the same socks or inserts as in the planning stage.

Do not turn a quick try-on into a durability claim. Record the date, duration and specific fit observations. If a size label or supplied item differs from the order, photograph the relevant label and the pair clearly. Repeat a measurement before treating a small difference as a defect. Keep the shoes in their received condition while checking the applicable support instructions; ordinary wear can change both the evidence and the condition of the item.

sections.title: Write a useful fit note and choose the next step
body: A useful fit note identifies the shoe, chosen size, measurement method and the result: for example, secure heel but pressure at the forefoot during a short indoor try-on. That illustrative wording describes an observation without recommending the same size to everyone. Avoid publishing personal order details or treating a size label as proof of authenticity. The review should help another reader understand your comparison, including its limits.

Use the general sizing guide for clothing measurements and the QC guide for a broader inspection of construction and images. If the wrong option arrived or the fit is unsuitable, consult the returns guide and the current order support path before sending anything back. A measurement-based method cannot guarantee comfort or a refund. It can make the choice more transparent and provide a clearer explanation when the delivered result differs from what you expected.

hacoo-refund-status.title: Hacoo Refund Status: Track a Pending Refund Step by Step
hacoo-refund-status.description: Separate a refund request, approval, return shipment, payment processing and receipt of funds so you can follow up on the right Hacoo order stage.

sections.title: Find the stage that is actually pending
body: A pending Hacoo refund can describe several different situations: a request awaiting review, an approved return waiting for shipment, a parcel awaiting receipt, a refund being processed or money not yet visible in the payment account. Start with the exact status shown for the order. Record its wording and date rather than shortening every unfinished stage to refund delayed.

This guide explains how to keep that record and prepare a focused follow-up. It does not provide access to your account or promise a processing deadline. Hacoo’s public return help directs customers to in-app support and the instructions for their case. The applicable order screen and support response therefore matter more than another shopper’s timeline. Keep the request, parcel and payment events separate, because completion of one does not automatically complete the others.

sections.title: A request is not the same as an approved refund
body: After submitting a request, keep the confirmation and the reason selected. Check whether the interface asks for additional evidence or shows a response deadline. A draft, an uploaded photograph or a message sent to support may not be a completed submission. Confirm that the request appears against the correct order and item before assuming it is being assessed.

Record any requested action in plain language: provide a clear label photo, explain the mismatch or wait for a decision. Send only relevant evidence through the official order channel. Do not submit several different reasons just to increase the chance of a favourable result; inconsistent descriptions make the timeline harder to understand. If the status is unclear, ask whether the request is complete and what specific information, if any, is still required.

sections.title: A return authorisation is a separate step
body: If the case requires a return, follow the address and instructions provided for that specific order. Do not send the item to the address printed on the original parcel unless support explicitly identifies it as the return destination. An approval to return an item is not necessarily a statement that money has already been issued. Record the authorised items, required packaging and any deadline shown.

Public guidance and individual resolutions can describe different return arrangements. Do not assume that every refund requires a return or that no refund ever requires one. Keep the actual instruction in the case record. Before dispatch, check the selected item, quantity and any documents that must accompany it. If the instruction conflicts with an earlier message, resolve the conflict in the same support thread before shipping the parcel.

sections.title: Track the return parcel independently
body: For a return that you have been instructed to send, keep the dispatch receipt and the carrier’s tracking reference privately. Record dispatch, the first carrier event, delivery and any acknowledgement in the order interface as distinct events. Carrier delivery is evidence about the parcel journey; it does not by itself prove that the contents were inspected or that a refund decision was completed.

If the tracking page and order screen disagree, explain that precise difference. For example, the carrier shows delivery on one date while the case still requests a return. Attach the relevant proof through support and ask which stage remains open. Do not describe the payment as missing when the actual pending step is acknowledgement of a return. That distinction makes the follow-up easier to route and avoids repeating evidence that has already been accepted.

sections.title: Check the amount and destination of an issued refund
body: When the order indicates that a refund has been issued or processed, record the amount, currency, date and stated destination. Compare those fields with the original transaction and the items covered by the resolution. A partial order resolution may not refer to every item in the cart. Do not infer the destination from a previous order; use the information supplied for the current case.

Keep product value, delivery charges, discounts and any other components separate when checking an amount. This is a reconciliation method, not a claim that any particular fee must be refunded. If a component is unclear, ask for a breakdown of the approved resolution. Currency conversion can make a payment-account entry look different from a displayed order amount, so compare the recorded currencies and dates before concluding that the refund is incomplete.

sections.title: Issued funds and received funds are different observations
body: The platform’s processing status and your payment account are separate sources. Check the relevant transaction history for the stated refund destination and record what is actually visible. A notification, a temporary balance change and a completed credit can describe different stages. Keep any processing estimate provided by the order or payment provider with its source and date rather than applying a universal number of days.

If the stated processing window has passed, use the existing official support case to request confirmation of the amount, destination and available refund reference. Then follow the payment provider’s own enquiry process where appropriate. Do not share a full card number, security code or login credentials in a public message. The useful evidence is the relevant transaction, date and reference, handled through the intended private support channel.

sections.title: Use a short timeline for the follow-up
body: A clear timeline can fit into five lines: request submitted, decision received, return sent if required, return acknowledged if applicable, and refund issued or received. Mark missing events as pending instead of inventing dates. If no return was required, say so and keep the instruction that supports it. This makes the record reflect the actual resolution rather than a generic process copied from another order.

Add one sentence describing the current mismatch and one concrete request. For example: the order says issued, but no matching credit is visible at the stated destination; please confirm the processing date and reference. That is an illustrative message structure, not a report about your account. Keep follow-ups in the same case unless support directs otherwise, and include only new evidence or the detail needed to identify the unresolved step.

sections.title: Close the record when the result is confirmed
body: When funds appear, compare the amount and currency with the resolution and record the date. If a balance or component remains disputed, keep that separate from the part already completed. Do not label the whole matter resolved simply because a support message arrived, and do not label every stage failed because one part remains open. The final note should describe the actual outcome without predicting how other cases will be handled.

Use the returns guide before preparing a request, the order-tracking guide for the original delivery and this guide for the later refund timeline. For a sizing issue, keep the selected option and measurement evidence with the case. A structured record does not guarantee approval or faster processing, but it prevents confusion between submission, authorisation, return receipt and payment. That clarity is the most useful starting point for deciding who should answer the next question.
